scope: Operational wrapper source preservation and bounded continuation; no new mathematical or kernel validation

findings.finding: Malformed, unreadable, or wrong-shape compiler receipt raises before the compiler outer row is retained and before mandatory post custody. Missing status has same effect.
findings.derivation: After subprocess.run returns, json.loads/read_text/native[status] raises; outer except records launcher-failure and reraises, bypassing next post iteration.
findings.recommendation: Guard receipt read, decode and status validation; preserve bounded failure details and compiler exit row; attempt post after compiler attempt whenever remaining budget and terminal ownership permit. Record explicit incomplete custody when post cannot be attempted.

findings.finding: RuntimeMaxSec bounds service running time but no explicit TimeoutStopSec or bounded launcher wait is specified. Shutdown/wait can exceed phase and cumulative ceiling before elapsed checks run.
findings.derivation: subprocess.run has no timeout; elapsed tests occur only after systemd-run --wait returns. TERM handler and blocking native filesystem operations can delay termination; default stop grace is not pinned.
findings.recommendation: Pin stop grace and charge it within phase allowance. Bound launcher wait and stop/kill/reap reconciliation within reserved cleanup time; preserve receipt on failure. Never start another phase if service termination is unconfirmed; record unresolved ownership and stop. Do not claim SIGKILL guarantees terminating uninterruptible I/O.

preserved_obligations: Fresh exclusive persistent workspace and exclusive phase markers
Full fresh pre and post dictionaries, realpath/stat/hash checks and equality
Runtime and source pins around compiler
Exact named axiom multiset with allowed axioms only
Malformed/duplicate/sorry parser guards and intended unsolved-goals negative rejection
Prior timeout and zero compiler invocations remain recorded
Failed pre stops compiler; no retries
Parent publication and runtime admission remain separate
